subject: SLO readout + load rehearsal logistics (customer-led)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Bryant <matt.bryant@northstar.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLO readout + next steps: load rehearsal planning

Hi Matt / Sarah —

Great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything aligned for the customer-led rehearsal:

Summary of targets you confirmed on the call:
- Non-streaming (request-response) p95 latency target: <= 500 ms (single-turn, 2k token cap).
- Streaming (websocket) time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target: p50 <= 200 ms; sustained streaming concurrency target: 100 concurrent streams, with short peaks to 150.
- Sustained throughput: ~70 requests/sec (baseline); peak bursts up to 120 req/sec for short windows.
- Long-form multi-turn runs will use a 4k token window; expect KV cache warm-up during ramp.

What we need from you to execute the customer-led run:
1) Confirm final test window(s) — we proposed Fri 2027-05-24 15:00-17:00 PDT during the call. Please confirm.
2) Provide the exact k6/Locust script(s) you plan to run (or a link to them). If you plan to use k6, send the script bundle and any custom JS modules.
3) Test account & ephemeral API key request: we will provision a dedicated test key with an isolated quota and observability hooks.
4) IP allowlist: please share the egress IP ranges you will originate from so we can pre-provision allowlist entries.
5) Test goals: please confirm whether you plan to exercise streaming endpoints or only classic non-streaming calls in the first rehearsal. If streaming, include max stream duration and average message size.

Redwood notes / recommendations for the rehearsal:
- For streaming runs, avoid KV cache pre-warm on the first ramp to see cold-start behavior, then run a warm-up phase.
- Recommend a 20-minute warm-up at 30% of target concurrency before ramping to full load.
- For k6, set thresholds for 95th latency and also track bytes/sec and websocket message loss.

Next steps: once you confirm the script and window we will provision the test account, push the IP allowlist entries, and send back a short runbook/checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to the rehearsal.

—
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
From: Matt Bryant <matt.bryant@northstar.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@northstar.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO readout + next steps: load rehearsal planning

Thanks Olga —

Confirming the proposed window: Fri 24 May, 15:00-17:00 PDT works for our ops team. A few clarifications / details on our side:

SLOs for engineering observability (what we'll validate):
- Non-streaming: p95 <= 450 ms (we'll test at 2k token payloads).
- Streaming: TTFB p50 <= 180 ms; sustained concurrency target 100, absolute max 150 concurrent streams.
- Throughput target: sustained ~70 req/s, ramp to 120 req/s within a 10-minute window.
- Error budget tolerance for rehearsal: up to 2% 5xxs accepted during short peak bursts.

We will run k6 for the non-streaming scenarios and a small Locust suite for streaming websocket validation. I'll attach our k6 bundle; Sarah will share the Locust config separately.

Attachments: northstar-k6-scripts.tar.gz (contains k6 script, payloads, ramp schedule).

We will originate traffic from the following egress ranges (shared by corporate infra):
- 35.198.12.0/24
- 34.102.45.128/25
- 104.154.32.0/22

For streaming tests expect average message size ~1.5KB, median stream duration ~90s. We'll want to validate reconnect behavior at scale as well.

Let us know what you need from Redwood.

Best,
Matt
Director, Platform Engineering
NorthStar Analytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLO readout + next steps: load rehearsal planning

Forwarding NorthStar details. Ben / Lauren — can you action the infra items below so we can lock the runbook?

Summary of asks from customer (from Matt):
- Test window: 2027-05-24 15:00-17:00 PDT
- Egress IP ranges to allowlist: 35.198.12.0/24, 34.102.45.128/25, 104.154.32.0/22
- k6 bundle attached from customer; Locust config coming separately
- SLOs: non-streaming p95 <= 450ms; streaming p50 TTFB <= 180ms; concurrency 100 sustained / 150 peak
- Throughput: sustained 70 req/s, peak bursts to 120 req/s

Internal asks: 
1) Ben — please create an isolated test API key for NorthStar that:
   - is rate-isolated from production (test quota ~200 req/s),
   - has logs forwarded to the NorthStar-facing dashboard,
   - includes streaming websocket endpoint access.
2) Lauren — can you provision the allowlist entries in the customer routing plane and confirm any autoscaler overrides needed to guarantee capacity for the two-hour window?
3) Ben/Lauren — attach whatever short runbook/checklist we want to ship to the customer before the run (k6 health checks, warm-up instructions, rollback steps).

Internal notes for infra:
- Recommend enabling request-level tracing for this key (sample 25%) and ensuring token-level cost breakdowns are visible to the customer during the run.
- For streaming, disable aggressive KV cache eviction for the rehearsal; want to measure steady-state streaming latency.

I'll send a consolidated runbook back to NorthStar once you confirm these items.

Thanks,
Olga

Thanks — I can take this. Quick updates:

1) Test credentials / key: created an ephemeral test API key (NS-TEST-20270524). Provisioned quota: 250 req/s (headroom vs requested). Key metadata and brief creds file attached (redwood-test-account-creds.txt). DO NOT share the raw key outside the run team.

2) IP allowlist: I pushed the three ranges to the customer routing plane (allowlist-ip-ranges.txt attached). They should be live in ~10 minutes. Please confirm once Matt says they see green on their side.

3) k6 wrapper: I adapted the customer's k6 bundle to include a small wrapper that toggles streaming vs non-streaming endpoints and reports token counts. See k6-wrapper-config.json attached.

4) Observability hooks: request traces will be sampled at 25% for this key; per-route dashboards are pre-created for NS rehearsal. We'll expose the dashboard link to Matt for live monitors.

5) Notes on limits: We set a temporary autoscaler override for the rehearsal window to ensure we don't fall back to lower-capacity nodes; ops will revert the override after the window. Lauren, I left the override until 18:00 PDT on the 24th — please rollback if not needed.

Attachments: redwood-test-account-creds.txt, allowlist-ip-ranges.txt, k6-wrapper-config.json

Thanks Matt — all set on our side. Quick final checklist and links before the run:

Runbook highlights (attached runbook-checklist.pdf):
- Warm-up: 20 minutes at 30% target concurrency to exercise KV warming and tracing.
- Ramp profile: 10-minute ramp from 30% -> 100% sustained; 5-minute burst to peak.
- Validation: monitor p95 latency, streaming TTFB, 5xx rate, token/sec counters.
- Rollback: pause traffic and fail traffic to a lower QPS model variant if 5xx > 3% for more than 5 minutes.

Credentials & access: Ben created the ephemeral key NS-TEST-20270524 and the allowlist entries should be live. Ben: please share the test dashboard link once it's visible (or confirm it is).

Customer artifacts: we have your k6 bundle in the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-northstar-k6). Please confirm the path to the main entry file so we can validate the wrapper.

Final ask: Reply to confirm the two things below so we consider the rehearsal locked:
1) Confirm you will run both k6 (non-streaming) and Locust (streaming) during the window.
2) Confirm you will start the warm-up 20 minutes before the scheduled start.

If everything checks out we will treat Fri 2027-05-24 15:00 PDT as confirmed and post the runbook to the Drive folder.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to it.

—
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
